newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia-Belarus Slavneft to reconstruct refinery.
newsitem.headline: Russia-Belarus Slavneft to reconstruct refinery.

text.p: Mozyr refinery, part of the Russian-Belarus oil company Slavneft, signed a contract with Britain's Euro Petroleum Consultants Ltd to design cracking equipment at the refinery, Slavneft said on Monday.

The refinery is undergoing reconstruction, planned to be complete by 2001, Vice-President Vladimir Zdobnov said last week. The reconstruction will raise the conversion level of the refinery to 70-80 percent from the current 50 percent, he added.
The Belarus government estimates the cost of reconstruction works at $300 million.
He did not say how high the credits would be, but said Slavneft and Mozyr refinery would fund some of the reconstruction themselves.
As part of financing, Slavneft will sell two percent of its shares in the near future, he said.

Slavneft's biggest sharesholders are the Russian State Property Committee with 45 percent, the Russian Federal Property Fund with over 32 percent, Belarus State Property Ministry with 10.8 percent and Mozyr refinery with 6.2 percent.
The Belarus government owns 42.7 percent in Mozyrsky Neftepererabatyvayushchi Zavod, Slavneft owns 42.6 percent.
